title: Agent Observability Aggregate Batch (v1)
description: Privacy-first aggregate telemetry batch, embedded unchanged in the desktop app's team shard. Carries ONLY pre-aggregated, non-sensitive measures bucketed by a fixed dimension grain. additionalProperties is false at every object level so a validator REJECTS any unexpected (potentially raw/sensitive) field. This is the single shared contract between the producer that builds the batch and the importer that validates it.

schemaVersion.description: Contract version. The API rejects any value other than '1.0' for this schema.

batchId.description: Deterministic idempotency hint for the whole batch. Computed by the producer as a hash of (pseudonymousDeveloperId + window.start + window.end + schemaVersion). It is at most an optimization for byte-identical retries: the API MAY skip re-processing an identical batchId, but correctness is guaranteed by per-row upsert on rowKey (latest-wins), NOT by batchId dedup. A repeated batchId carrying corrected/fuller buckets (e.g. late-arriving spans) MUST still re-apply row upserts; the API must never silently drop a batch solely because batchId was seen before.

generatedAt.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the producer built this batch. Informational only; not part of any idempotency key.

toolVersion.description: Semantic version of the app that produced the batch (e.g. '1.4.2'). Used for compatibility diagnostics and schema-drift triage.

pseudonymousDeveloperId.description: Opaque, stable developer identifier: literal 'dev_' prefix + 32 lowercase hex chars (first 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(salt, normalized git email)). The strict pattern structurally excludes emails, usernames, and any free text — an email or PII value cannot satisfy ^dev_[0-9a-f]{32}$. MUST NOT be reversible without the org salt (which is never transmitted). See pseudonymization-strategy.md. Used by the consumer as the distinct-count dimension for 'active developers'.

window.description: The closed-open UTC time range [start, end) that all buckets in this batch fall within. Defines the slice of local telemetry the producer has aggregated.

start.description: Inclusive UTC start of the covered range (ISO 8601).

end.description: Exclusive UTC end of the covered range (ISO 8601). MUST be greater than start.

buckets.description: Pre-aggregated rows. Each element is one fully-summarized row at the dimension grain (bucketStart, bucketDurationSeconds, repository, model, agentMode, operation, toolName?). An empty array is a valid heartbeat batch indicating activity-free time.

bucket.description: One aggregate row at grain (bucketStart, bucketDurationSeconds, repository, model, agentMode, operation, toolName?) for a single pseudonymousDeveloperId. All measures are additive across rows EXCEPT distinctSessionCount and the dimension distinct-counts, which must be recomputed by the consumer (see doc).

rowKey.description: Stable per-row idempotency key. Hash of the full grain tuple (bucketStart, bucketDurationSeconds, repository, model, agentMode, operation, toolName) + pseudonymousDeveloperId. A consumer upserts by rowKey so re-sent or overlapping windows converge to the same row instead of double-counting.

bucketStart.description: Aligned UTC start of the time bin (ISO 8601). In v1 bins are ALWAYS aligned to 30-minute boundaries (minutes ∈ {00,30}, seconds=0, ms=0). All interactions in this row started within [bucketStart, bucketStart + bucketDurationSeconds).

bucketDurationSeconds.description: Width of the time bin in seconds. v1 GLOBAL INVARIANT: const 1800 (30 minutes), matching the existing overview RequestVolume query bin(TimeGenerated,30m) exactly so no resolution is lost. Because bin width AND alignment are globally fixed (not just per-batch), rowKeys for the same wall-clock window always collide and upserts converge — re-binning at a different width would be a breaking change requiring a schemaVersion bump, never a re-send.

repository.description: SANITIZED git remote, resolved per session (COALESCE of copilot_chat.repo.remote_url across the session, else literal 'unknown'). CRITICAL PRIVACY RULE: the producer MUST normalize to 'https://{host}/{owner}/{repo}' form — stripping any userinfo (the 'user:token@' / 'x-access-token@' segment that git remotes can embed, which would leak PATs/credentials), any query string, and any fragment, and dropping a trailing '.git'. The pattern enforces this structurally by forbidding '@', whitespace, '?', and '#'; a credential-bearing URL cannot satisfy it. SSH remotes (git@host:owner/repo) MUST be converted to the https host/path form. May be replaced by a salted hash in a future schema version.

repositoryBranch.description: OPTIONAL and OMITTED by default. Source: copilot_chat.repo.head_branch_name. Privacy tradeoff: branch names can leak feature/customer/ticket identifiers, so the producer omits this unless an org explicitly opts in. Never required by the API.

model.description: Resolved model identifier (COALESCE of gen_ai.response.model / gen_ai.request.model), or 'unknown'. Non-sensitive.

agentMode.description: Copilot chat mode (copilot_chat.mode_name), defaulting to 'default' when absent. PRIVACY NOTE: custom chat mode names are user-defined and could embed project/customer identifiers, so the producer MUST map any mode not in the known set {default, ask, edit, agent} to the literal 'custom' before sending. Only the mapped value appears here.

operation.description: OTEL operation_name / gen_ai.operation.name of the spans aggregated into this row.

toolName.description: OPTIONAL. Present only when operation = 'execute_tool'. Source: gen_ai.tool.name (e.g. 'read_file', 'run_in_terminal'). PRIVACY NOTE: built-in Copilot tool names are passed through verbatim, but third-party/MCP tool names are vendor-defined and could embed identifiers, so the producer maps any tool name outside the known built-in allowlist to 'custom'. Tool arguments/results are NEVER included.

interactionCount.description: Total spans aggregated into this row (additive across rows). Maps to LogAnalytics 'Requests' / TotalRequests.

successCount.description: Count of spans with OTEL status_code in {0=unset, 1=ok} (additive). Used to derive success rate.

errorCount.description: Count of spans with OTEL status_code = 2 (error) (additive).

inputTokens.description: Sum of input_tokens over chat spans in this row (additive). Feeds model usage InputTokens.

outputTokens.description: Sum of output_tokens over chat spans in this row (additive). Feeds model usage OutputTokens.

cachedTokens.description: Sum of cached_tokens (gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens) over chat spans (additive).

reasoningTokens.description: OPTIONAL. Sum of reasoning_tokens over chat spans (additive). Omitted when the model/provider does not report reasoning tokens.

durationMsSum.description: Sum of span durations in milliseconds (end_time_ms - start_time_ms) (additive). Average latency = durationMsSum / interactionCount, computed by the consumer after merging rows. A raw average is intentionally NOT shipped because averages are not additive.

latencyHistogram.description: Fixed-bound duration histogram enabling mergeable approximate percentiles (e.g. p95) by the consumer. Counts are additive bound-for-bound.

distinctSessionCount.description: Number of distinct sessions (COALESCE(conversation_id, chat_session_id)) observed within THIS row only. WARNING: NOT additive across rows; the consumer uses it only for per-row context. True distinct session totals over a range require by the consumer distinct counting (see doc).

lastActivityAtMs.description: OPTIONAL. Unix epoch milliseconds of the latest span start_time_ms aggregated into this row (max over the row). Lets the consumer recover a last-seen time at true event resolution (taking the max across a developer's rows) rather than degrading it to the 30-minute bucketStart. Non-sensitive (a timestamp).

latencyHistogram.description: Fixed-bound latency histogram. boundsMs are the upper bounds (exclusive of the next bucket) in milliseconds and MUST equal the shared canonical bounds so histograms from different rows/developers can be merged element-wise. counts has length boundsMs.length + 1: the final element is the '+Inf' overflow bucket for durations greater than the largest bound.

boundsMs.description: Canonical shared upper bounds in milliseconds. MUST be exactly [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 30000] in v1 so all rows are mergeable.

counts.description: Per-bucket counts, additive across rows. Length is boundsMs.length + 1 (= 9). counts[i] for i < boundsMs.length is the number of spans with duration <= boundsMs[i] and > boundsMs[i-1]; counts[last] is the +Inf overflow (duration > 30000ms).
